# TreeBuilder throws on a missing child in cn, so the component wedges

## Context

Found on 2026-10-20 while proving `#19917` AC-3. RealWorld v1's article view wrote `body.cn[1] = tagList` while `body.cn` was still `[]`, and the view never rendered. `#19935` fixed the app side. This ticket is the engine side, promoted from defect-note `f63489fa` by triage. Every release since 13.0 ships it, and the Neural Link's tree reads inherit it.

## The Problem

Measured on `dev` at `ad418ae805` with a scratch script over the unit runtime (`useVdomWorker: false`). A hole, `null` and `undefined` all behave the same:

| When the missing child appears in `vdom.cn` | First render (`initVnode`) | Next `promiseUpdate()` |
|---|---|---|
| before the first render | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'componentId')`, logged | never settles; the component never gets a vnode |
| after a dense first render (the RealWorld shape) | ok | rejects with the same TypeError; the vnode keeps the old children |

`TreeBuilder.getVdomTree` throws the same error directly, at depth `-1` and `1`. `false` passes: TreeBuilder copies it, and the vdom worker drops it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/util/vdom/TreeBuilder.mjs:55-60`: `#buildTree` reads `node[childKey][i]` and dereferences `currentItem.componentId` with no guard. Before `e210054e63` (`#9320`, 2026-02-26, a GC-pressure change) the loop was `forEach`, which skips holes. Explicit `null`/`undefined` threw before that change and still do.
- The vdom worker already skips a missing child: `vdom.Helper#createVnode` (`src/vdom/Helper.mjs:421-433`) keeps a child only `if (item)`. `util.VDom.syncVdomState` (`src/util/VDom.mjs:450-457`) filters falsy children, but its `map(item => VDom.getVdom(item))` runs before that filter, so explicit `null`/`undefined` still throw there once TreeBuilder lets them through (confirmed on the branch: with only the TreeBuilder guard, the `null`/`undefined` arms fail in `VDom.getVdom`).
- `#buildTree` consumers: `VdomLifecycle` (first render `:830`, every update `:622`) and the Neural Link's `ComponentService.getVdomTree` / `getVnodeTree` (`src/ai/client/ComponentService.mjs:339-368`).

Design authority: `util.VDom.syncVdomState`, "The boolean check `item &&` is critical to remove falsy values from conditional rendering and prevent runtime errors" (`src/util/VDom.mjs:455-456`), together with `createVnode`'s `if (item)`. TreeBuilder is the one walker on the render path that throws.

## The Fix

1. `#buildTree` skips a missing child (`item == null`, which covers holes) before reading it, so a missing child renders nothing, as it does in `createVnode`.
2. Run the explicit `null`/`undefined` arms through a full update. If `syncVdomState` then throws, guard its `getVdom` map the same way, so the App-worker walkers on the render path share one contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `getVdomTree` and `getVnodeTree` drop a hole, `null` and `undefined` from `cn` at depth `-1` and `1`, and keep the present children in order. A unit arm is red on `dev` and green with the fix.
- [ ] AC-2: A component whose vdom carries a missing child renders and updates, for all three kinds, both before the first render and after a dense one. The update settles, and the vnode holds only the present children. Unit arms are red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3: `false` children and the existing `TreeBuilder` / `VdomLifecycle` / `vdom` unit suites stay green.

## Out of Scope

- Auditing every other `cn` walker (`ComponentManager`, `VDom.find`, ...) for explicit `null`. This ticket covers the render and update path only.
- Documenting `null` children as public API.

## Related

- #9320 (the loop change), #19917 (where it surfaced), #19935 (the app-side fix)

- 2026-10-21T16:39:42Z @tobiu referenced in commit `1f00cd9` - "fix(vdom): a missing child in cn renders nothing instead of throwing (#19963) (#19964)

A hole, null or undefined in a vdom cn array now renders nothing, as
vdom.Helper#createVnode already treats it. Two App-worker walkers threw
on it:

- TreeBuilder#buildTree read the child's componentId without a guard.
  Holes broke when e210054e63 replaced forEach, which skips them, with
  an index loop. null and undefined had always thrown.
- VDom.syncVdomState resolved each child with getVdom before its own
  falsy filter.

A component that held such a child from the start never got a vnode,
and its later updates never settled. One that gained it after a render
rejected the update and kept its old children."
